definition.description: Sit tall on a clean stable mat or floor with both legs extended in a declared comfortable straddle. Reach forward through a comfortable controllable range without forcing a passive hold, then return to the same tall seated straddle before the next repetition. One forward reach and tall return is one repetition. Pause and reset between repetitions. Range, reach target, breath, tempo, repetitions, rest, surface, and cueing are delivery annotations. Static straddle folds, any leg lift or compression drill, pike folds, supine trunk lifts, loaded work, assessments, and clinical interventions are different tasks requiring their own reviewed variant or definition.

athleteSupport.whyItMatters: Practises a controlled straddle reach and clear tall return without forcing range or turning it into a leg lift.
athleteSupport.primaryCue: Sit tall, reach only as far as you control, then return tall before the next repetition.
secondaryCues: keep both legs extended in your declared straddle
breathe instead of forcing the reach
make the range smaller if the tall return changes
expectedSensations: gentle inner- and back-of-thigh lengthened-position sensation
unexpectedSensations: dizziness, nausea, chest symptoms, unusual breathlessness, numbness, tingling, weakness, or circulation change
selfChecks: legs stay extended in declared straddle
no forced range, bouncing, or leg lift

observationChecklist: exact seated straddle reach-to-tall cycle, not static pancake, pike, or compression lift
tall start and finish, leg and knee position, range, tempo, breath, symptoms, and first quality loss

faultCorrections.forced_range: reduce reach and restore controlled tall return; do not chase range
faultCorrections.collapsed_tall_return: shorten reach and pause tall before another repetition
faultCorrections.leg_lift: stop and reset; lifting is a different task with separate review

exact straddle reach conflicts with current symptoms, restrictions, floor access, or communication

snapshot.description: Seated in a straddle, reach forward with a long spine, then practice lifting one or both legs slightly while maintaining upright trunk. Alternate reaches and lifts at low amplitude.
